lines.text: 50/50 bills can take a much bigger bite from one paycheck.
lines.say: Fifty-fifty bills can take a much bigger bite from one paycheck.

lines.text: Example: you take home $6,000 a month, your partner $4,000, and bills are $3,000.
lines.say: Example: you take home six thousand a month, your partner four thousand, and bills are three thousand.

lines.text: Split 50/50, that's $1,500 each: 25% of one paycheck, 37.5% of the other.
lines.say: Split fifty-fifty, that's fifteen hundred each: twenty-five percent of one paycheck, thirty-seven point five percent of the other.

lines.text: By income, it's 60/40: $1,800 and $1,200, 30% of each paycheck.
lines.say: By income, it's sixty-forty: eighteen hundred and twelve hundred, thirty percent of each paycheck.

lines.text: Same $3,000 either way: one splits the dollars, the other splits the percentage.
lines.say: Same three thousand either way: one splits the dollars, the other splits the percentage.

lines.text: Per Pew, 71% of opposite-sex marriages in 2022 had one spouse earning over 60% of the pay.
lines.say: Per Pew, seventy-one percent of opposite-sex marriages in twenty twenty-two had one spouse earning over sixty percent of the pay.

lines.text: In 2025, full-time women's median weekly pay was 82.1% of men's, per the BLS.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, full-time women's median weekly pay was eighty-two point one percent of men's, per the B L S.

lines.text: A 2024 UK YouGov poll found 46% of working couples split 50/50, 38% by income.
lines.say: A twenty twenty-four UK YouGov poll found forty-six percent of working couples split fifty-fifty, thirty-eight percent by income.

post.title: Splitting bills 50/50 vs by income: the math on $3,000
post.ig:
50/50 bills can take a much bigger bite from one paycheck.
Example: $6,000 and $4,000 take-home, $3,000 in shared bills. 50/50 = $1,500 each = 25% vs 37.5% of pay. By income (60/40) = $1,800 and $1,200 = 30% of each paycheck.
Pew: in 2022, 71% of opposite-sex US marriages had one spouse earning over 60% of the couple's pay.
BLS: full-time women's median weekly pay was 82.1% of men's in 2025.
YouGov (UK, 2024): 46% of working couples split 50/50, 38% split by income.
Sources: Pew Research Center (2023), BLS Usual Weekly Earnings (2025 annual averages, 11 months), YouGov (2024).
